text:
maya: Quick question for the group: how should inference sidecars propagate sampling decisions and billing metadata when a single user request fans out to multiple model calls?

jordi: do you mean the HTTP frontdoor -> sidecar -> multiple model shards pattern?

maya: exactly. today each model call emits a separate trace/span and billing event. Customers are asking for a single logical trace and consolidated cost line.

sam: two pieces: trace stitching (to present one logical trace) and cost attribution (to avoid double-billing). They are related but can be decoupled.

trent: naive approach: keep original request_id on all spans and have sidecars emit a parent span at frontdoor. But that doesn't fix per-model billing since each model may report tokens independently.

ashley: what if sidecar emits a single consolidated billing event with per-model deltas? Sidecars can sum token estimates locally and send one ack to billing with breakdown.

jordi: downside: central billing loses visibility into model-level consumption unless we include per-model microrecords. That increases cardinality.

maya: alternative: sampling-based consolidation. Sidecar picks one model invocation per request as the canonical billing emitter (deterministic hash on request_id mod n) and others emit marker-only. Central billing reconstructs via markers.

sam: risk: complexity and risk of undercount if markers are lost. Need marker reliability SLA. Also makes per-model charge noisy unless we sample per-model separately.

trent: operationally, we could support two modes: consolidated-billing (sidecar sums and emits one invoice line) and model-detailed (emit per-model). Tenant opt-in via deployment flags. Default = consolidated for cost visibility and lower cardinality.

ashley: for traces, we can still emit full per-model spans but annotate them with request_id and parent_span_id so the UI can stitch. UI can optionally collapse model spans into a logical grouped view.

jordi: also add a reconciliation path: if customer disputes a bill, enable a debug window where sidecars stream raw, per-model events for the disputed window.

maya: good. what about sampling decision propagation? If frontdoor samples 1% of traces, sidecars should honor it so we maintain consistent sampling ratio. We'll carry a sampling_decision header with deterministic TTL.

sam: agree. header name: x-rwin-sample: {decision:keep|drop, seed:hex, version:1}. Sidecars must be idempotent when decision=drop but still emit a minimal marker for metrics.

trent: security: ensure sampling headers are signed or have HMAC so tenants cannot spoof. Use gateway shared key per deployment.

ashley: perf note: consolidating billing in sidecars adds CPU on hot paths. We'll prototype in a canary cluster and measure p95. If too heavy, push consolidation to a post-processing aggregator that groups related model calls by request_id.

maya: action items: 1) draft RFC with modes (consolidated/model-detailed), header spec for sampling, UI stitching behavior, and backfill/replay playbook. 2) prototype sidecar consolidated billing + sampling header. 3) SRE to add debug replay flow.

infra-bot: Ticket INF-7601 created to track sidecar billing modes and sampling propagation.

maya: assigning owners: maya (RFC + prototype), jordi (UI stitching), sam (billing reconciliation), trent (security HMAC header), ashley (perf canary). We'll review next Tuesday. Thanks all!
